summary: @servicetitan/help-center 1.0.9 ships preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload
details: The package's package.json declares a preinstall hook that runs setup.mjs, which downloads the Bun runtime (bun-v1.3.13) from GitHub releases into a temp directory, extracts it, chmods it executable, and then invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js bundled at the package root. math_init.js is a ~727 KB Bun-compiled bundle using string-array + rotation obfuscation (shuffle function WV8StW, hex-random identifiers, large mixed constant table) with no readable content and no functional relationship to the advertised purpose of the package (React components for a help-center micro-frontend). Bun is not a declared runtime dependency of a React component library, and setup.mjs also falls back to a bundled ZIP parser if unzip/powershell are unavailable and will reuse an already-installed local bun binary if present, ensuring the payload executes across environments. The advertised React/MobX component code under dist/ and src/ is unrelated to and does not invoke this install-time chain. The dropper fires automatically on npm install via the preinstall lifecycle hook, running attacker-controlled obfuscated code on the installer's machine under a freshly fetched second-language runtime chosen to evade Node-oriented static scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
